memories.text: We deploy the api service with a canary that takes 5% of traffic for 20 minutes before full rollout, because the March 2026 outage reached every customer within two minutes of a direct rollout.
The production Kubernetes cluster is named tl-prod-euw1 and runs in the europe-west1 region.
The staging cluster tl-stage-euw1 is rebuilt from scratch every Sunday at 03:00 UTC, so nothing stateful may live there.
Helm upgrades of the api chart fail with 'field is immutable' if the Deployment's selector labels change; the selector must be left as app.kubernetes.io/name=api.
Every Helm release name equals the chart name plus the environment, for example api-prod or worker-stage.
Rollbacks are done with helm rollback to the previous revision, never by redeploying an older image tag by hand, so the release history stays truthful.
The deploy window for production was Tuesday and Thursday 09:00 to 15:00 CET until 2026-05-31.
Since 2026-06-01 production deploys are allowed Monday to Thursday 09:00 to 16:00 CET; Friday deploys stay forbidden.
The worker pods need terminationGracePeriodSeconds of at least 120, otherwise invoice PDF jobs are killed mid-render during a rollout.
The ingress controller is ingress-nginx 1.11 and terminates TLS with certificates issued by cert-manager from Let's Encrypt.
Cert-manager renewal failed silently in August 2026 because the ClusterIssuer's ACME account email pointed at a deleted mailbox.
Container images are tagged with the full git commit SHA, never with latest, so a running pod can be traced back to its commit.
The api Deployment runs 6 replicas in production with a HorizontalPodAutoscaler that scales between 6 and 18 on 65% CPU.
kubectl port-forward to the production database is blocked by a NetworkPolicy; use the bastion pod db-bastion in the ops namespace instead.
We chose Argo CD over Flux in January 2026 because Argo's UI let the on-call reviewer see drift without cluster credentials.
Argo CD syncs the tl-prod-euw1 cluster from the deploy/prod directory of the infra repository every three minutes.
Argo CD marks the api application OutOfSync forever if the HPA changes spec.replicas; the Deployment manifest must omit replicas.
Node pools in production use e2-standard-8 machines; the pdf-render pool uses c2-standard-16 because rendering is CPU bound.
After moving pdf rendering to the c2-standard-16 pool, the p95 invoice render time fell from 4.1 s to 1.7 s.
Secrets reach pods through the External Secrets Operator from Google Secret Manager; no secret is ever committed to the infra repository, even encrypted.
An ExternalSecret refresh does not restart pods; after rotating a secret, run kubectl rollout restart on the Deployment that mounts it.
The blue-green switch for the marketing site is a Cloud DNS record change with a TTL of 60 seconds.
Database migrations run as a Kubernetes Job named migrate-<sha> before the api rollout starts, and the rollout waits for the Job to succeed.
Pod startup takes 38 seconds on average, of which 30 seconds is the JVM warming the invoice template cache.
The primary database is PostgreSQL 16 on Cloud SQL, instance tl-pg-prod, with one synchronous standby in a second zone.
Before the upgrade the database ran PostgreSQL 13; the upgrade to 16 happened on 2026-03-14 with 11 minutes of write downtime.
After the upgrade to PostgreSQL 16, the nightly ledger aggregation query got 3x faster because of incremental sort.
After the PostgreSQL 16 upgrade, run ANALYZE on every table, because pg_upgrade does not carry planner statistics and the first day's plans were terrible.
Every table has a created_at and updated_at column of type timestamptz, set by the database, never by the application.
We use UUIDv7 primary keys instead of bigserial so ids sort by creation time and can be generated by clients before insert.
Adding a column with a volatile default rewrites the whole table; on the invoices table that took a lock for 9 minutes in staging.
Indexes on large tables are created with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, and the migration must not run inside a transaction for that statement.
The invoices table holds about 410 million rows and is partitioned by month on issued_at.
Old monthly partitions of invoices older than 7 years are detached and exported to cold storage, because the retention law requires 7 years.
The connection pooler is PgBouncer in transaction mode with a pool of 80 server connections per database.
With PgBouncer in transaction mode, session-level SET statements and prepared statements leak between clients; use SET LOCAL inside a transaction.
The ledger_entries table had 31% bloat in July 2026 because autovacuum could not keep up with updates to the status column.
Ledger entries are append-only: a correction is a new reversing entry, never an UPDATE, so the ledger can be audited.
Point-in-time recovery for tl-pg-prod is configured with 14 days of WAL retention.
The read replica lags up to 40 seconds under the nightly batch, so reports that must be exact read from the primary.
Migration files live in db/migrations and are named with a timestamp prefix like 20260314_0930_add_tax_region.sql.
The tax_rates table is keyed by (country_code, region_code, valid_from) and the lookup takes the latest valid_from not after the invoice date.
A missing index on payments(invoice_id) caused sequential scans that added 800 ms to the invoice detail page; the index was added on 2026-04-02.
jsonb columns compared with = treat key order as irrelevant, but the text cast does not; never compare jsonb::text in queries.
Row level security is enabled on every tenant table and filters by current_setting('app.tenant_id').
A connection that never set app.tenant_id sees zero rows rather than an error, so a missing tenant context looks like an empty account.
We do not use database triggers for business logic; triggers are only allowed for updated_at and audit rows.
Database backups are taken nightly at 01:00 UTC and copied to a bucket in a second region, tl-backups-euw4.
The restore drill on 2026-09-10 restored tl-pg-prod into a scratch instance in 47 minutes.
The public API is versioned in the URL path; v2 is current and v1 is deprecated with a sunset date of 2027-01-31.
Every API error response is a JSON object with code, message and request_id fields, and the code is a dotted string such as invoice.not_found.
Pagination uses opaque cursors rather than page numbers, because offsets over the partitioned invoices table were slow and unstable under inserts.
The default page size is 50 and the maximum is 200; a larger limit is refused with request.validation.
The Idempotency-Key header is required on POST /v2/invoices; a retry without it creates a duplicate invoice.
Idempotency keys are remembered for 24 hours; a reuse after that creates a new resource.
Handler functions are named verb_resource, for example create_invoice, list_payments, void_credit_note.
The rate limit is 600 requests per minute per API key, enforced by a token bucket in Redis, answering 429 with Retry-After.
Most 429 responses in September 2026 came from one integration partner polling GET /v2/invoices every second instead of using webhooks.
Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body and the timestamp, using a per-endpoint secret, and receivers must reject signatures older than 5 minutes.
Webhook signature checks fail if the receiver parses and re-serializes the JSON before hashing; the signature covers the raw bytes.
Webhook delivery retries with exponential backoff for up to 72 hours, then the endpoint is disabled and the account owner is emailed.
The OpenAPI document is generated from the handlers by utoipa and published at /v2/openapi.json.
Money amounts in the API are integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code, never floats: amount_minor=1999, currency=EUR.
Currencies with three decimal places, such as KWD and BHD, break code that assumes minor units are cents; use the currency's exponent.
The API uses ISO 8601 timestamps in UTC with a trailing Z; local times are never accepted or returned.
The api service is written in Kotlin on Ktor 2.3 and runs on Java 21.
Switching the JSON library from Jackson to kotlinx.serialization cut p50 latency of GET /v2/invoices/{id} from 42 ms to 31 ms.
kotlinx.serialization drops fields with default values from the output unless encodeDefaults is true, which silently removed status=draft from responses.
Request timeouts are 30 seconds at the ingress and 25 seconds in the Ktor server, so the server answers before the ingress cuts the connection.
User login uses OpenID Connect with Auth0 as the identity provider; the tenant id travels in a custom claim https://tallyline.example/tenant.
API keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes with a visible 8 character prefix like tl_live_ab12cd34, and the full key is shown once at creation.
Auth0 access tokens expire after 1 hour but the console kept a stale token in localStorage, so users saw 401 errors after lunch until the refresh fix.
Permission checks happen in the service layer with requirePermission(), never in controllers or SQL.
Roles are owner, admin, accountant and viewer; only owner can delete the organization or change billing.
We rejected storing session tokens in cookies without SameSite=strict after the CSRF finding in the June 2026 pentest.
The June 2026 penetration test found a CSRF hole on POST /settings/members because the session cookie used SameSite=lax.
Auth0 rate limits the Management API to 15 requests per second; bulk user imports must be throttled or they fail halfway.
Two-factor authentication is mandatory for owner and admin roles since 2026-07-01.
Never log full API keys, tokens or passwords; the logger's redact filter masks fields named token, secret, password and authorization.
Service-to-service calls inside the cluster use mTLS through the Linkerd mesh rather than shared bearer tokens.
Linkerd's mTLS is skipped for traffic to the database port because the proxy is configured to skip port 5432; database TLS is enforced by Cloud SQL instead.
Signing keys for JWTs issued by the api are rotated every 90 days and published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
An expired JWKS cache in the worker caused all webhook-triggered jobs to fail authorization for 25 minutes on 2026-08-19.
Personal data of end customers is encrypted at the field level with envelope encryption under a Cloud KMS key per tenant.
Deleting a tenant's KMS key makes its encrypted fields unrecoverable after the 30-day destroy schedule; that is the GDPR erasure path and must never run by accident.
Security findings are tracked as issues with the label security and must be fixed within 7 days for high severity and 30 days for medium.
The SSO feature for enterprise plans supports SAML 2.0 through Auth0 enterprise connections.
The customer console is a React 18 single-page app built with Vite and TypeScript, deployed to Cloud Storage behind Cloud CDN.
React components use PascalCase file names, such as InvoiceTable.tsx, and hooks start with use, such as useInvoiceFilters.ts.
Server state is managed with TanStack Query rather than Redux, because almost all state is a cache of API responses.
TanStack Query refetches on window focus by default, which tripled API traffic from the console; refetchOnWindowFocus is now false for list queries.
The console's design system is in packages/ui and is published to the internal npm registry as @tallyline/ui.
The console bundle was 2.4 MB gzipped in May 2026; lazy-loading the reports module brought the initial bundle down to 780 kB.
Intl.NumberFormat with style currency rounds JPY to zero decimals, so the console must not append a hard-coded .00.
All user-facing strings go through the i18n function t() with keys in locales/en.json; German and French are the other shipped locales.
Dates in the console are displayed in the organization's time zone, not the browser's, because accountants share screens across offices.
End-to-end tests for the console use Playwright and run against the staging environment on every merge to main.
Playwright tests flake when they click the invoice row before the virtualized table has measured rows; wait for data-ready=true first.
Sentry showed 40% of console errors in October 2026 came from a browser extension injecting scripts, not from our code; those are now filtered by allowUrls.
Feature flags in the console come from LaunchDarkly and are read through the useFlag hook.
Form validation uses zod schemas shared with the API client generated from openapi.json.
The generated API client must be regenerated with npm run gen:api after any API change, or TypeScript types silently drift from the server.
CI runs on GitHub Actions; the main workflow is .github/workflows/ci.yml and must pass before merge.
The api service builds with Gradle 8.7 and the Kotlin 1.9.24 compiler.
The Gradle build cache in CI is keyed on gradle/libs.versions.toml; changing a dependency version invalidates the whole cache and the build takes 14 minutes instead of 4.
We require two approving reviews on the api repository and one on the console, because api changes reach money.
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits, for example fix(api): refuse negative invoice totals.
Container images are built with Docker Buildx and pushed to Artifact Registry at europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/tallyline/images.
The integration tests use Testcontainers and need Docker; they fail on the macOS runners, so the job is pinned to ubuntu-24.04.
The flaky test InvoiceNumberingTest.concurrentIssue failed 6% of runs because two threads raced on the numbering sequence; it was fixed with SELECT FOR UPDATE.
A test that flakes is quarantined with the @Flaky annotation and an issue link within one day, never just retried.
Dependabot opens dependency update pull requests every Monday, grouped by ecosystem.
Renovating ktor from 2.3 to 3.0 is blocked because ktor 3.0 needs Kotlin 2.0 and our kapt annotation processors do not support K2 yet.
We stay on Kotlin 1.9 until the kapt processors are replaced with KSP, planned for Q1 2027.
Static analysis runs detekt for Kotlin and eslint for TypeScript; a new detekt finding fails the build.
Release tags follow semantic versioning with a v prefix, such as v4.12.0, and each tag builds and publishes a release image.
The SBOM for every image is generated by syft and attached to the GitHub release as sbom.spdx.json.
The GitHub Actions cache is limited to 10 GB per repository, and the Gradle and npm caches together evict each other on busy days.
Moving the npm install step to pnpm with a shared store cut the console's CI time from 9 minutes to 5 minutes.
The console uses pnpm 9 and Node 20 LTS, pinned in .nvmrc and packageManager in package.json.
Merges to main are squash merges only, so main's history has one commit per pull request.
Self-hosted runners were removed in 2026 because a fork pull request could run code on them; never re-enable pull_request_target with checkout of the head.
The analytics pipeline exports invoices and payments nightly from PostgreSQL to BigQuery dataset tl_analytics with Datastream.
dbt models for analytics live in the analytics repository under models/marts, and run at 05:00 UTC after the export.
Revenue metrics are computed in dbt, not in the application, so finance and the product dashboard read one definition.
Datastream converts PostgreSQL numeric columns to BigQuery BIGNUMERIC, and dbt models that cast them to FLOAT64 lose cents.
dbt model names are prefixed by layer: stg_ for staging, int_ for intermediate, fct_ and dim_ for marts.
The monthly recurring revenue model is fct_mrr_daily and is the source for the board's MRR chart.
fct_mrr_daily double-counted upgrades in August 2026 because the plan change event was emitted twice; dedup on event_id fixed it.
BigQuery charges by bytes scanned; queries on tl_analytics.invoices must filter on the partition column issued_date or they scan 900 GB.
The churn model labels an account churned after 45 days without a paid invoice.
Product events are sent to Segment and land in BigQuery; we decided not to send them to the operational database to keep it small.
Segment's identify calls from the console sent the user email as the user id until 2026-05; those rows must be excluded from user-level analyses.
Airflow 2.9 on Cloud Composer orchestrates the pipeline; the main DAG is nightly_finance_pipeline.
The nightly_finance_pipeline DAG missed its 07:00 SLA four times in September 2026 because the Datastream backfill after the schema change took 3 hours.
A schema change to a table exported by Datastream needs a heads-up in the #data channel one day before, so the backfill can be scheduled.
Data retention in BigQuery is 25 months for raw event tables; aggregated marts are kept indefinitely.
dbt incremental models with unique_key on a partitioned table do a full merge scan unless incremental_predicates limits the target partitions.
Personal data is pseudonymized in the stg_ layer with a salted hash, and only the finance service account can read the salt.
Looker is the BI tool; its LookML project reads only the marts, never staging tables.
Invoice numbers are sequential per organization and per year, formatted like INV-2026-000123, because several EU countries require gapless numbering.
A voided invoice keeps its number; issuing a replacement takes the next number, never reuses the voided one.
Credit notes are separate documents that reference the original invoice, instead of editing an issued invoice, because issued invoices are legally immutable.
VAT is calculated per line and rounded half-up to the currency's minor unit, then summed, as German tax rules require.
Rounding the invoice total instead of each line gives a different VAT amount by up to one cent per line; accountants reject those invoices.
Reverse charge applies to B2B invoices inside the EU when the buyer has a valid VAT ID; the invoice then shows 0% VAT and the note 'Reverse charge'.
VIES VAT ID validation is down for some member states for hours at a time; we accept the ID and re-validate later rather than block invoicing.
Payments are collected through Stripe; card and SEPA Direct Debit are supported, and SEPA payments settle after up to 5 business days.
A SEPA Direct Debit can be charged back up to 8 weeks after collection, so an invoice paid by SEPA is not final until then.
Dunning sends reminders at 3, 10 and 21 days after the due date, then suspends the account at 30 days.
Moving the first reminder from 7 to 3 days after the due date reduced average days-to-pay from 19 to 14.
Subscription plans are Starter, Growth and Scale, billed monthly or yearly; yearly plans get two months free.
Proration on a mid-cycle plan upgrade is computed by Stripe; our own preview must call Stripe's upcoming invoice endpoint rather than estimate.
Stripe objects are referenced by their Stripe id in a column named stripe_<object>_id, such as stripe_customer_id.
Stripe webhooks are received at /hooks/stripe and verified with the Stripe signing secret before any processing.
Stripe can deliver the invoice.paid event before checkout.session.completed, so handlers must not assume event order.
E-invoices for Italian customers are sent through the SDI exchange in FatturaPA XML format via the provider Acube.
XRechnung and ZUGFeRD support for German public sector customers is scheduled for Q2 2027, not before.
Metrics are scraped by Google Managed Prometheus and dashboards live in Grafana at grafana.ops.tallyline.example.
Logs are structured JSON written to stdout and shipped to Cloud Logging, kept 30 days.
Every log line carries request_id, tenant_id and service; a log without request_id fails the logging lint in CI.
Traces use OpenTelemetry with the OTLP exporter to Cloud Trace, sampled at 10% except errors which are always kept.
Alerts page only on symptoms customers feel (error rate, latency, failed payments), not on causes like CPU, to avoid alert fatigue.
The api SLO is 99.9% of requests answered without a 5xx over 30 days, with p95 latency under 300 ms.
The error-rate alert ignores 429 responses; a partner flood of 429s once hid a real outage behind a quiet dashboard, so 429 has its own alert now.
On-call rotates weekly on Monday at 10:00 CET through PagerDuty, with one primary and one secondary.
Every alert must link a runbook in the runbooks repository, and an alert without a runbook is not merged.
Half of the pages in Q3 2026 were the DiskPressure alert on the pdf-render pool, which was noise; it was downgraded to a ticket.
Prometheus counters reset when a pod restarts; use rate() or increase(), never raw counter values, in dashboards.
Uptime checks probe https://api.tallyline.example/healthz from three regions every minute.
High-cardinality labels such as tenant_id are forbidden on Prometheus metrics; per-tenant numbers come from logs instead.
Adding invoice_id as a metric label in July 2026 created 2 million series and the Prometheus bill grew fivefold in a week.
The 2026-03-02 outage was caused by a direct rollout of an api image with a broken database migration; all requests failed for 34 minutes.
The 2026-08-19 incident: webhook-triggered jobs failed for 25 minutes after a signing key rotation because the worker cached the old JWKS for 24 hours.
After the 2026-08-19 incident the JWKS cache lifetime was cut to 10 minutes and a key is published 24 hours before it signs.
The 2026-10-07 incident: invoice emails were delayed by 6 hours because the SendGrid API key was rotated but the ExternalSecret was not refreshed in the worker.
Every incident with customer impact gets a blameless postmortem within 5 business days, stored in the postmortems folder of the runbooks repository.
The 2026-09-23 slowdown came from a reporting query that took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock through an accidental ALTER TABLE in a migration.
During an incident, the status page at status.tallyline.example must be updated by the incident commander within 15 minutes of declaring it.
Severity levels are SEV1 (all customers down or money wrong), SEV2 (a feature down for many customers) and SEV3 (degraded, workaround exists).
The 2026-05-12 double charge: 214 SEPA mandates were charged twice because a retried batch job had no idempotency key.
Batch payment jobs must pass an idempotency key per invoice to Stripe since the 2026-05-12 double charge.
When refunding the double-charged customers, refunds over 10000 EUR needed manual approval in Stripe and stalled the bulk script.
The 2026-06-30 DNS incident: the marketing site went down for 50 minutes because the domain's auto-renewal card had expired.
Do not run destructive SQL (DELETE, UPDATE without WHERE, DROP, TRUNCATE) against tl-pg-prod from an agent session; open a change request instead.
Never deploy to production on a Friday or on the day before a public holiday in Germany.
Do not add a new runtime dependency to the api without a short note in the pull request on why the standard library or an existing dependency is not enough.
Do not edit generated files such as the OpenAPI client in packages/api-client by hand; regenerate them.
Never store customer invoice PDFs in a public bucket; the invoices bucket tl-invoice-pdfs is private and served through signed URLs that expire after 15 minutes.
Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in docs/adr with the number, a title sentence and the rejected alternatives.
Pull requests stay under about 400 changed lines; a larger change is split into a stack.
The team works in two-week sprints starting on Wednesdays; planning is Wednesday 10:00 CET.
Branch names start with the issue number, such as 1432-dunning-sepa-retry.
The api repository's code owners for billing code are the billing crew; changes under src/main/kotlin/billing need their approval.
Do not use floating point types for money anywhere in the code base; use Long minor units or BigDecimal.
The invoice_service.rs prototype in Rust was abandoned in April 2026 because the team's Kotlin expertise outweighed the latency gain of 8 ms.
The function compute_line_vat in billing/VatCalculator.kt is the single place VAT per line is computed.
The InvoiceRenderer class renders PDFs with OpenPDF 1.3.30 and embeds the Noto Sans font for non-Latin scripts.
Upgrading OpenPDF past 1.3.30 changed default line spacing and shifted totals onto a second page for long invoices; pin it until the template is fixed.
The environment variable TL_PDF_CONCURRENCY controls how many invoice PDFs a worker renders at once; the default is 4.
